summary: In international space defense, the U.S. Space Force and Japan launched a second military payload to bolster space surveillance over the Indo-Pacific region. The deployment comes as the European Union imposed new sanctions targeting leaders of Russia’s space industry, and China completed back-to-back Long March launches—placing a satellite into orbit for the United Arab Emirates—to recover from a recent rocket explosion. In commercial news, United Launch Alliance named Peller as its new CEO, while L3Harris appointed Sam Mehta as chief executive following the removal of Christopher Kubasik over a conduct violation. On the pad, SpaceX set a record by launching two Falcon 9 rockets 38 minutes apart, and Blue Origin began adding a second pad to its Cape Canaveral launch complex while repairing explosion damage. In defense contracting, the U.S. Air Force tested portable ground stations for Collaborative Combat Aircraft, and defense agencies selected three companies for satellite deorbiting design studies. For civil space, NASA selected contractors for payload processing services, funded preliminary studies on spherical aerobots to explore caves on Saturn's moon Titan, and marked the Curiosity rover's 14th landing anniversary on Mars. In astronomy, observations from the Hubble Space Telescope resolved an early Milky Way merger mystery, while researchers cataloged the mega-Earth exoplanet GJ 523b and identified multiple colliding supermassive black hole candidates. Readers should keep an eye on Japan as it advances plans for a mission targeting the moons of Mars.
